R0273.title: VLA Model Backdoor & Training-Data Poisoning
R0273.definition: The risk that an attacker implants backdoors in VLA training/fine-tuning data or imitation-learning demonstration data so the robot performs attacker-specified actions under specific trigger conditions.
R0273.description:
VLA model backdoor and training-data poisoning has become an independent research direction. DropVLA (action-level backdoor, OpenVLA-7B) makes reusable action primitives execute at attacker-chosen decision points; only 0.31% poisoned samples achieve 98.67%–99.83% attack success while retaining over 98% clean-task performance. BadVLA (NeurIPS 2025) is the first untargeted VLA backdoor. State Backdoor uses the robot arm's initial state as a trigger, with over 90% success. BEAT uses environmental objects to trigger visual backdoors. AgentPoison targets RAG-based autonomous-driving agents; poisoning less than 0.1% achieves over 80% ASR. Imitation-learning demonstration-data poisoning makes the robot learn wrong or dangerous policies from the source; stealthy samples are visually indistinguishable from benign images and can bypass manual review.

This risk relates to R0243 (training-data poisoning risk), but R0243 focuses on general-AI training-data poisoning while this risk is specialized for VLA-model backdoor triggers and the embodied-policy layer, emphasizing physical-action triggers.
R0273.influence: Robots lie dormant long-term and perform dangerous actions under specific triggers (e.g., unlocking or attacking when a specific visual patch appears); backdoors are highly stealthy and hard to detect, and supply-chain poisoning can affect all downstream deployed robots.
